I made a few updates to my lean game yesterday and attempted to push them to the server this morning. As far as I can tell the import went fine but the effect was to delete the game. Can anyone help me figure out what happened? I'm planning to mention it in a talk tomorrow at TYPES and would love to have it back by then.

Note that the game link still works but it looks like a blank Lean Game. The old entry for my game on the landing page of the Lean game server has now disappeared.
Here's a screenshot of what happened after the import

I've actually tried importing twice this morning to see if this would help, the most recent time after some cosmetic edits to the explanatory text and the library (attempting to add a few new theorems). This second round of editing resulted in some weird behavior locally. When I ran localhost:3000 I could see the edits I made last night but not the edits I made this morning. Maybe the problem was caused by lake build not building the right files, since no changes were made to the Lean code?

Gemini seemed to think the issue might be with the container so I went back to the GameSkeleton repo and attempted to copy across the various file directories suggested there. This just made the problem worse because now localhost:3000 doesn't show anything at all (though it did 20 minutes ago).
The uncommitted diff looks something like this:
I can roll these changes back if they were a mistake. So the main issue is the failure to import to the Lean game server.
I think the game metadata was accidentally removed in 741aba1, my guess is that's the issue, PR incoming in a moment once GitHub stops acting slow...
https://github.com/emilyriehl/ReintroductionToProofs/pull/24
Looks like it's back up -- hope in time for your talk!
Thank you so much. I feel like an idiot. I wonder how I managed to do that?

Now that we're back online, folks might enjoy the new boss level for advanced function world. There's no game-specific knowledge needed here. The aim is to prove a fun result from category theory called Lawvere's fixed point theorem, which abstract Cantor's proof of diagonalization.
@Emily Riehl , Thank you for the game! I really enjoyed it. If I ever teach Lean, I’d like to try using it.
I'm glad it's working again:blush: Thanks Julian!

I'm back with another issue with my game that I can't figure out...

For some reason the introductory text to EquivalenceWorld does not display.

I don't know when this issue started. The Game.lean file looks fine as far as I can tell. The most recent change I made involved some fiddling with namespaces. A couple of the levels (not all) are in a custom ReintroductionToProofs namespace. So that the functions defined there are usable later, I opened this namespace in a few subsequent levels. (I suspect putting those levels in the namespace would have been better, but this was quicker. It would also have been better to implement this change uniformly.)

Could that have caused this issue? If not, how do I fix it. Apologies again...

Also in EquivalenceWorld,

  1. After completeng Level 6/8 the text is "completed! :tada:
    We are now ready for the Boss Level of Equivalence World."
    But now the Boss level should be Level 8?

  2. Both levels 7 and 8 are called Boss levels with identical introductory texts (in fact, for level 7).

@Emily Riehl you cannot import a specific level of some world in another world, only entire worlds. Likely you have a import MyGame.EquivalenceWorld.LevelXy somewhere in a file that's defining a level outside EquivalenceWorld. This is a long standing issue which manifests in an empty world introduction. You can fix it by replacing it withimport MyGame.EquivalenceWorld

Could you check if that could be the issue? If it's not then I'd need to look at the code

As the name suggests this L08 is not imported into Game.Levels.EquivalenceWorld so does not display. When I manually cut it from Game.lean the EquivalenceWorld landing text reappeared.
But anyway my question: what should the top of Game.lean look like?

In case it helps, here's how the set theory game is set up:
Game.lean imports all of the world files:

import Game.Levels.Subset
import Game.Levels.Comp
import Game.Levels.Inter
import Game.Levels.Union
import Game.Levels.Combo
import Game.Levels.FamInter
import Game.Levels.FamUnion
import Game.Levels.FamCombo

Then each world file imports all of the levels of that world. For example, the imports of Game.Levels.Subset.lean look like this:

import Game.Levels.Subset.L01exact
import Game.Levels.Subset.L02subhyp
import Game.Levels.Subset.L03have
import Game.Levels.Subset.L04imp
import Game.Levels.Subset.L05subref
import Game.Levels.Subset.L06subtrans

Then it gets a little more complicated to explain. The first world is Subset World, and the first level, Game.Levels.Subset.L01exact.lean, imports Game.Metadata. Each level after that imports the previous level. For example, Game.Levels.Subset.L02subhyp.lean imports Game.Levels.Subset.L01exact. For the other worlds, the first level imports the previous world (that is, the last world it depends on), and every level after that imports the previous level. For example, Game.Levels.Comp.L01contra.lean imports Game.Levels.Subset, and Game.Levels.Comp.L02compdef.lean imports Game.Levels.Comp.L01contra.

I don't know if that's the recommended way of doing it, but it works. There's some redundancy here; each world file could import just the file for the last level of that world, since each level after the first imports the previous one, but it seemed clearest for each world file to import all of its levels.

Emily Riehl said:

But anyway my question: what should the top of Game.lean look like?

I think this should be fine (besides the import which isn't present in the world file). The usual setup is what Dan writes.

I think the bug is that if you import import Game.Levels.EquivalenceWorld.L08_UnusedBossLevel at top level but not inside import Game.Levels.EquivalenceWorld then the env extension might store an empty EquivalenceWorld (with no Intro) and when the world is actually defined it doesn't override it, so you end up with an empty intro text.

(btw: I assume your autogenerated file comes from lake exe mk_all, not lake build)

@Dan Velleman Regarding importing previous levels , I think I setup knights and knaves at first to do this, but now all i do is

import Game.MathlibTheorems
import Game.LevelLemmas.dsl_KnightsAndKnaves

at the top of every level

MathlibTheorems has imports like Mathlib.Tactic.Have , GameServer.Commands

LevelLemmas.dsl_KnightsAndKnaves defines a namespace with all the necessary setup and defintions , axioms , theorems etc...

So , importing the previous level/world is not the only way to make things work.(I don't know which is the recommended way of doing things either...)
